content.intro: This lesson studies Data Manipulation and Presentation within APIs, Asynchronous Operations, and Data Handling. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Remote data can fail, arrive late, or become stale, so data fetching needs explicit cancellation, retry, and empty-state behavior.

content_blocks.title: Data Manipulation and Presentation: Reactive dependency flow
content_blocks.alt_text: Reactive dependency flow diagram for lesson 85: Data Manipulation and Presentation. Change a ref or reactive property → Track dependencies; derive or run side effects → Vue schedules the required render update
content_blocks.caption: Reactivity flow: track the state that changes, choose computed values for pure derivation, and use watchers for side effects.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: API integration coordinates asynchronous JavaScript, HTTP requests, server data, loading/error states, and configuration across environments. This lesson focuses on Data Manipulation and Presentation. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Filtering and sorting
items.text: For Filtering and sorting, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: Search and computed results
items.text: For Search and computed results, identify the reactive source that changes and the value or side effect that depends on it. Prefer computed values for derived data; use watchers when a change must trigger work outside pure derivation, and keep dependencies explicit.

items.title: Formatting dates and currency
items.text: For Formatting dates and currency, bind the input to a clear state value, validate before submission, and associate field errors with their controls. A disabled or loading state should be reflected in the UI without treating the client as the authority for server validation.

content_blocks.expected_output: On success, the console prints an array of user objects. Network access or the example service may be unavailable, so failure is explicitly caught.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use in a browser-compatible module or component method. Prefer a local fixture for automated tests and check HTTP status before parsing business data.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Data Manipulation and Presentation with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Search and computed results”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: API integration coordinates asynchronous JavaScript, HTTP requests, server data, loading/error states, and configuration across environments. For Data Manipulation and Presentation, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Data Manipulation and Presentation” that applies “Filtering and sorting”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Filtering and sorting”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.
